defect_observations.note: The power section presents Holm's ten-normal example (cited pp.67-68) with recomputed values 0.4412670349 and 0.5631999191. It never reports the source's printed 0.439 and 0.565 (journal p.68; holm-1979-extracted.txt lines 320-322) and does not explain the difference. This is about fidelity to the source, not a coverage gap: the comparison and its direction are present.

Several source remarks are not carried. From p.67 (extracted lines 284-303): (a) except in trivial cases, the sequentially rejective test has strictly larger probability of rejecting false hypotheses; (b) the power gain depends on the alternative, small when all hypotheses are 'almost true' and large when some are 'completely wrong', which reduces to Holm on the remaining hypotheses. The body gives only 'These inequalities need not be strict' (line 151). Also missing: the p.68 remark that the power increase from the independence-based variant is not very big (extracted lines 419-420), and the p.70 closing remark that independence of the statistics is desirable for design rather than computation (extracted lines 597-610). None of these is an element of an owed success condition.

The claim 'Independence solely at the complete null is insufficient for strong control' has no proof or construction. The annex (lines 365-390) proves only the positive result and d_k > alpha/k. Failure item 3 (body 469-472; annex 502-509) places the dependence at the complete null itself, so it does not show a model where complete-null independence holds and strong control still fails. The claim is outside the owed components.

In the strong-control proof, the referent of 'that true hypothesis' is ambiguous. The step from 'some true hypothesis is rejected' to 'the comparison at the first true rank j is passed' comes from the prefix characterization in the body (lines 94-95: H^(r) is rejected exactly when every comparison j<=r passes). The proof does not restate it. Minor: the proof steps are present.
